title: FinPerMA: A Theory-Informed, Event-Grounded Personalized-Memory Benchmark for LLM Agents
title_zh: FinPerMA：一个理论驱动、事件锚定的 LLM Agent 个性化记忆基准
abstract_en: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly used as personalized assistants in high-stakes domains such as financial advising, yet it remains unclear whether they can maintain and update an individualized user model over long horizons. Existing personalized-memory benchmarks primarily test factual retention or rely on weakly constrained model-generated trajectories, leaving event-driven preference adaptation underexplored. We introduce FinPerMA, an event-grounded benchmark that evaluates personalized memory against frozen longitudinal investor trajectories. Its generation pipeline combines deterministic, theory-informed impact rules, controlled LLM narration, and automated quality screening; a Post-Shock checkpoint isolates whether an agent has integrated a material event into its persistent user model. On 2,994 questions from 276 personas, seven frontier LLMs and up to seven memory configurations remain far from saturated: no full-context configuration exceeds approximately 0.47 overall accuracy or approximately 39% on multiple-choice questions. Attribution analysis shows that summary-based memory often preserves factual details while losing the preference signals needed for personalization; simple retrieval can therefore outperform purpose-built memory systems, with the gap widening after shocks.
abstract_zh: 随着 LLM agents 越来越多地用于金融建议等高风险个性化助理场景，模型能否在长时间跨度内维护并更新个体用户画像仍不清楚。现有个性化记忆基准多关注事实记忆，或依赖约束较弱的模型生成轨迹，较少评估事件驱动的偏好变化。本文提出 FinPerMA，一个基于冻结纵向投资者轨迹的事件锚定基准，用于评估个性化记忆能力。其生成流程结合了确定性的理论驱动影响规则、受控 LLM 叙事生成和自动质量筛选；其中 Post-Shock 检查点专门用于判断 agent 是否已将重大事件整合进持久用户模型。作者在 276 个 persona、2,994 个问题上评测了 7 个前沿 LLM 和最多 7 种记忆配置，结果显示当前系统远未饱和：即使使用完整上下文，总体准确率也不超过约 0.47，多选题准确率不超过约 39%。归因分析表明，基于摘要的记忆常能保留事实细节，却会丢失个性化所需的偏好信号；因此，简单检索有时反而优于专门设计的记忆系统，且该差距在冲击事件后进一步扩大。
key_points_zh: 提出 FinPerMA，用于评估 LLM agents 在金融投资建议场景中的长期个性化记忆与偏好更新能力。
基准构建基于冻结的纵向投资者轨迹，结合理论驱动的确定性影响规则、受控 LLM 叙事和自动质量筛选。
设计 Post-Shock 检查点，专门检验模型是否能在重大事件后更新持久用户画像与投资偏好。
在 276 个 persona、2,994 个问题上评测 7 个前沿 LLM 及多种记忆配置，完整上下文设置下总体准确率仍仅约 0.47。
实验发现摘要式记忆易保留事实但丢失偏好信号，简单 retrieval 在冲击事件后可能优于专门记忆系统。

llm_assessment.comment: A valuable personalized-memory benchmark focused on event-driven preference adaptation, though its financial domain narrows direct reuse.
llm_assessment.comment_zh: 这是一个有价值的个性化记忆基准，聚焦事件驱动的偏好适应，但金融领域设定限制了直接复用范围。
